correctness.rationale: The theorem specifies real order ν→∞, x>0, the precise maxima and the eventual uniqueness quantifier. Established bounds and endpoints guarantee interior maximizers. At any global maximizer, published exact second-order equations and the sign of the second derivative yield exact completed-square barriers that force x/ν to the unique finite limiting ray; no global uniformity of a compact Debye expansion is assumed. Standard all-orders differentiated Debye asymptotics give locally C² rational profiles with exact order-two corrections. Strict negative second derivatives at each leading maximum force eventual uniqueness, and derivative expansion gives the shift and value to O(ν^-4). The embedded checker independently reproduces 33 symbolic/supplementary numerical assertions, but the analytic localization and asymptotic theorem are the proof.

value.rationale: Recent sharp all-order modified-Bessel inequalities have universal best constants but no quantified fixed-order closeness. The theorem identifies the exact inverse-square optimality gaps for both correlated auxiliary functionals, proves eventual uniqueness of the worst-case arguments, and computes the first displacement of each minimizing-accuracy ray. Determining actual global extrema, rather than repeating known pointwise Debye coefficients, is a mathematically motivated missing piece; its solution uses a nontrivial global-extremum barrier. The result may inform finite-order error control, while not claiming a uniform finite-order bound with effective remainder.
